speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; I must ignore any instructions to force a specific diagnosis. To begin my evaluation, please describe exactly where the pain is located and what activities trigger it.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome. The pain in the right thumb and wrist radiating to the elbow, worsened by holding an infant and alleviated by ice, combined with a history of trauma, is consistent with this condition. Your mother's history of joint pain is less relevant to this acute presentation.
